summary: Discovery call focused on migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Customer runs PHI-bearing inference for clinical notes and is concerned about latency, cost, eval parity with current models (OpenAI + local vLLM fallback), and compliance (HIPAA, SOC2). Redwood AE/SE covered Dedicated offering, private/VPC options, KMS integrations, and recommended benchmark plan and POC to validate eval parity and latency/cost targets.
topics: model compatibility and eval parity (OpenAI vs Redwood-hosted models)
security/compliance: HIPAA, SOC2, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~38 mins
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (CTO, Sentinel Health), Ravi Desai (Head of ML), Ellie Park (Security), Tom Lewis (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Sentinel's current reliance on OpenAI for inference, their experiments with vLLM/TGI for on-prem inference, and whether Redwood Dedicated or Private is the right fit given HIPAA constraints and strict latency SLAs.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - uh - really appreciate it. I'm Alex Rivera, AE on the account, with Samir and Jia from solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya: Doing well, thanks. We've got a lot to cover. Sorry for the slightly later start - runway on another sync.
[00:10] Ravi: Yeah hi, Ravi here. We run the ML stack, will focus on throughput and eval parity.
[00:14] Ellie: Ellie from security - I'll be listening for compliance details.
[00:18] Alex: Great. Goal today is to understand your current setup and blockers for moving off OpenAI hosted endpoints into either Redwood Dedicated or our private offering. We'll also cover POC mechanics if that seems like a fit.
[00:30] Samir: Quick intro from me - I'm Samir, SE - I handle performance, deployment, and benchmarking. Happy to jump into latency/cost questions.
[00:38] Tom: Tom - infra, current network configs and peering questions.
[00:42] Alex: Cool, Maya do you want to kick off with where you're at and what your needs are?
[00:46] Maya: Sure. High-level, Sentinel provides clinical summarization and triage tools; a lot of the prompt/data touches PHI so we need HIPAA controls. Right now prod uses OpenAI API - mostly gpt-4 style endpoints - but costs are getting insane and we see some latency variance. We also have a team experimenting with vLLM and TGI on-prem for edge cases, but it hasn't matched the quality of the OpenAI models. So primary questions: can Redwood Dedicated match eval parity? Can we get predictable latency and cost? And what are the compliance guarantees - like can we have VPC-only, bring-your-own-key, and audit logs?
[01:25] Alex: Totally. That's the bread-and-butter. Short answer: Dedicated can give predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale, plus VPC/private control plane options for PHI. KMS/HSM integrations for customer-managed keys are supported. We have audit logs and can run SOC2 + HIPAA attestation packages.
[01:40] Ellie: What's the scope of the HIPAA attestation - is Redwood willing to sign a BAA? Also, where does the data persist - any message retention?
[01:48] Jia: We do standard BAAs for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can sign a BAA and the platform can be configured with zero retention for prompts and responses at rest if required. We'll share the exact wording in the security docs but yes - BAA + KMS control + configurable retention.
[02:05] Ravi: On model compatibility - we currently call OpenAI and have a suite of eval prompts. We also tried local vLLM with Llama 3 quantized, but the outputs diverged. How do you handle model variants and eval parity?
[02:20] Samir: Good question. We onboard both curated open models and provide Redwood-verified performance profiles. For migrations from OpenAI, we run a parity eval during POC: we recommend 10-20k representative prompts, run through your OpenAI baseline and candidate models on Redwood Dedicated, and compare metrics like exact match, ROUGE, hallucination rates, and token-level latency. We also support model pinning so you can pin a variant that passes your quality bar.
[02:46] Maya: And what about vLLM/TGI compatibility - can we bring our own runtime? We liked vLLM for local caching and KV cache optimizations.
[02:55] Samir: We support standard model formats and have runtime adapters. For Dedicated you can run our runtime on your hardware or use Redwood-managed Dedicated nodes. If you want to self-host the runtime with vLLM/TGI, we can validate compatibility, but note some optimizations (kernel selection, quantization-friendly paths) are specific to our runtime - which gives better latency/cost in many benchmarks.
[03:18] Ravi: So some moving parts: open model format compatibility is fine, but the execution path matters for latency and throughput. We need to test with our prompts.
[03:25] Samir: Exactly. That's why the POC benchmark is important. We'll propose a small Dedicated pool to run your evals with identical seq lengths and concurrency to mirror production.
[03:34] Tom: Network question - if we go Dedicated managed by Redwood, can we do VPC peering and restrict egress? We have strict egress rules for PHI.
[03:42] Alex: Yes - Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private offering has a customer-managed control plane option. We can also provide egress allowlists and SGs; we will need your infra diagram and egress rule set to draft the network runbook.
[03:56] Ellie: Encryption at rest and in transit - KMS? HSM?
[04:00] Jia: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can support HSM-backed keys in Private/on-prem deployments. TLS in transit is standard; for Dedicated we recommend customer-managed KMS for key exp control.
[04:15] Maya: Back to costs - do you have any ballpark numbers comparing OpenAI hosted and Redwood Dedicated for summarization workloads? Our prompts are ~600 tokens, responses ~800, heavy concurrency during peak hours.
[04:26] Alex: I'll send SKU+pricing but rough math: at scale, Dedicated unit economics can be 3-6x cheaper per token depending on batching and caching. We can show a modeled delta once we run your representative workload. Also Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/caching/quantization to reduce cost further.
[04:45] Ravi: Latency SLO - we need p95 under 450ms for short chat flows and p95 under 1.5s for longer summarization with 800 tokens. Can Dedicated hit that?
[04:56] Samir: For an 800-token completion p95 1.5s is aggressive; it depends on model size and hardware. If you use a tuned 30B or 70B quantized on A100/4xA100 or equivalent, we've seen steady p95 in that range with our runtime and KV caching for prefix reuse. For shorter prompts we can often do under 450ms for smaller models (7B-13B) depending on concurrency. We'll validate during POC with your exact models.
[05:22] Maya: We do want to avoid quality regressions; some of our clinical outputs are sensitive. Does Redwood have model eval tooling or rollbacks?
[05:30] Samir: Yes - rollouts, canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies. Also we store per-prompt quality metrics (you can integrate your evals) and set regression alerts. For POC we can help build the eval harness.
[05:45] Ellie: Audit logs - is there token-level logging for who invoked what? We need to be able to show access logs for audits.
[05:52] Jia: Audit logs with route-level traces and token-level cost breakdowns are part of the Console. For stricter setups, logs can be shipped to your SIEM via syslog or S3 with restricted retention.
[06:05] Tom: A few nitty-gritty infra items - do you support private endpoints and private DNS? And how do you handle upgrades/maintenance windows for Dedicated?
[06:16] Alex: Private endpoints + private DNS supported. For managed Dedicated we coordinate maintenance windows; we can run in multi-pod setup for zero-downtime. For Private/on-prem you control the upgrade cadence.
[06:28] Ravi: On model side, we call OpenAI's chat completions with function calling. How much work is it to port function calls and structured output expectations to Redwood?
[06:36] Samir: We support function/tool calling equivalents and structured output primitives; porting is generally straightforward - we provide SDKs and examples. We'll validate any edge cases in the POC.
[06:45] Maya: What about fallback strategies? We like the idea of online fallback to OpenAI in case Dedicated is overloaded during burst. Is that supported?
[06:52] Jia: Smart routing supports policy-based routing: prefer Dedicated, fallback to hosted variants (including OpenAI-compatible hosted) if latency or capacity issues occur. That can be configured per route.
[07:05] Ellie: Can we get a read on data residency - we need everything to remain in us-west-2 for now.
[07:11] Alex: Yes, we can pin regions for Dedicated and Private deployments. We'll note US-WEST-2 as a requirement for the POC.
[07:18] Maya: Great. Next, ops questions: how long to stand up a small Dedicated pool for a POC?
[07:24] Samir: If you're using Redwood-managed Dedicated, a small 2-4 GPU pool can be provisioned in a couple of weeks; Private/on-prem obviously depends on your procurement and imaging. For a real POC we'd propose a 2-4 week run to collect 10-20k eval prompts.
[07:40] Ravi: For the evals, can you run them head-to-head with our OpenAI traces without us sharing raw PHI? We can probably de-identify or synthetic the dataset.
[07:48] Samir: Yep - synthetic or de-identified traces are fine. We'll provide a benchmark template and a small harness that runs locally and pushes anonymized metrics back to Redwood for comparison.
[07:58] Tom: If we do VPC peering, what ports and IP ranges are needed?
[08:02] Alex: We'll create a network runbook but typical egress is over TLS to a small set of Redwood IPs - we'll ask you for your CIDR and egress policies and then return an allowlist.
[08:12] Maya: Any known blockers with Anthropic or Azure OpenAI migrations? We have a couple of endpoints there for experiments.
[08:19] Jia: No blockers - we support models that are functionally analogous. For Azure OpenAI specifically, data plane differences may exist; we recommend the same POC approach to ensure parity. Competitors and differences can be surfaced in the eval.
[08:32] Ravi: One small ask - we rely on vLLM for prefix caching for conversational flows. If we move to Redwood, how do we get equivalent prefix/KV cache behavior to keep token costs down?
[08:43] Samir: Redwood runtime implements KV cache and prefix caching; we can configure it for conversation reuse. In many cases, our batching + caching produces better cost curves than vanilla vLLM. We'll demonstrate with your conversation traces.
[08:58] Ellie: Security - will you provide a SOC2 attestation and penetration test summary?
[09:03] Alex: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we'll share the report redacted for third parties and pen test summary. For Private deployments you can request a full audit.
[09:12] Maya: Okay, great. Any immediate risks you see to migrating?
[09:16] Samir: Biggest risks are eval parity surprises and network constraints. Both are testable in a POC. If you have strict p95 SLAs, hardware sizing and model selection will be critical.
[09:27] Ravi: Sounds good. Let's talk timeline - we're targeting a pilot in late March/early April. Is that feasible?
[09:32] Alex: Yes, feasible. We'll coordinate a POC kickoff week of 3/16 and get the pricing + runbook to you earlier.
[09:38] Maya: Great. Quick recap?
[09:40] Alex: Recap: Redwood to send Dedicated pricing/SKU; Samir to send benchmark template and harness; Customer to de-id sample evals and send infra diagram; Redwood to share SOC2/HIPAA docs and network runbook; schedule POC kickoff week of 3/16.
[09:55] Ellie: Sounds right. Anything else?
[09:57] Tom: No, thanks. We'll pull together infra artifacts.
[10:00] Alex: Thanks all - we'll follow up via email with next steps.

End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional stutter and mis-heard technical names (e.g., vLLM sometimes transcribed as V-L-L-M, TGI as tee-gee-eye), some speaker attribution may be generic.
